related_questions.question: What is the life expectancy of someone with degenerative heart disease?

text_blocks.snippet: The life expectancy for people with degenerative heart disease, also known as heart failure, varies greatly depending on several factors, including the severity of the condition, age, and other health conditions. While some individuals may live for many years with proper management, others may face a significantly shortened lifespan.

list.title: Severity of Heart Failure:
list.snippet: The stage of heart failure significantly impacts life expectancy. In Stage D, or end-stage heart failure, life expectancy is typically less than a year, according to Mass General Brigham.

list.title: Age:
list.snippet: Younger individuals generally have a better prognosis than older individuals.

list.title: Other Health Conditions:
list.snippet: The presence of other conditions like diabetes, COPD, or kidney disease can negatively impact life expectancy.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Treatments like LVADs (left ventricular assist devices) and heart transplants can significantly extend life expectancy, even in advanced stages.

list.title: Lifestyle:
list.snippet: Factors like diet, exercise, and adherence to medication can also influence the course of the disease and life expectancy.
A 2019 review of over 1.5 million heart failure patients found that roughly 57% survive for 5 years after diagnosis, and about 35% survive for 10 years.
Some studies suggest that more than 50% of people with congestive heart failure may live for another 5 years from diagnosis.
A 2015 study found that the mean years of life lost due to heart failure was 9.64 years.
For those with end-stage heart failure, the median survival time is often around 6 to 12 months.
These are general statistics and individual outcomes can vary widely.
Early diagnosis and treatment, along with lifestyle modifications, can significantly improve the prognosis and quality of life.
Advances in medical technology and treatments are constantly improving the outlook for heart failure patients.
